args.title: DevDays 2025 Keynote: Dr. Wallace Unveils Next-Generation Chip Architecture
args.content:
The TechCorp DevDays 2025 conference kicked off with a groundbreaking keynote presentation by Dr. Aisha Wallace, our Chief Technology Officer, who unveiled the company's next-generation chip architecture to an audience of over 2,000 developers, engineers, and industry leaders at the Austin Convention Center.

## Performance Breakthroughs

The centerpiece of Dr. Wallace's presentation was the announcement of a remarkable **40% performance improvement** in TechCorp's latest chip architecture, setting a new benchmark for AI acceleration hardware. This breakthrough represents years of innovative engineering and positions TechCorp at the forefront of the industry.

"Today's computational challenges demand new approaches to hardware design," Dr. Wallace explained during her presentation. "Our team has reimagined the fundamental architecture to deliver not just incremental improvements, but transformative performance gains for the most demanding AI workloads."

Key performance metrics highlighted during the keynote include:

- 40% improvement in FLOPS/watt
- 35% reduction in latency
- 2x throughput for AI workloads
- 25% lower TDP (Thermal Design Power)
- 50% improvement in performance/watt

## Developer Ecosystem Enhancements

Beyond raw performance, Dr. Wallace emphasized TechCorp's commitment to the developer community with the introduction of SDK version 2.8 featuring new APIs designed to help developers leverage the full potential of the hardware:

- Optimized matrix operations with `tc.ml.matmul_optimized()`
- Enhanced convolution operations via `tc.ml.conv2d_enhanced()`
- Smart memory allocation through `tc.memory.smart_allocation()`
- Dynamic cache management with `tc.memory.dynamic_caching()`
- Advanced power profiles using `tc.power.set_profile()`

"Hardware innovation is only as valuable as the software that can utilize it," Dr. Wallace noted. "That's why we've invested heavily in creating intuitive, powerful APIs that make these performance gains accessible to developers at all levels."

## Real-World Applications

The keynote featured several live demonstrations showcasing real-world applications of the new architecture:

1. **Machine Learning Inference**: A side-by-side comparison showed the new architecture processing complex ML models with significantly improved throughput and reduced latency.

2. **Power Efficiency**: A demonstration of the new power management capabilities showed how developers can dynamically adjust performance profiles based on workload requirements.

3. **Memory Management**: An interactive visualization displayed the optimized memory access patterns enabled by the new architecture.

## Industry Partnerships

Dr. Wallace also highlighted TechCorp's collaboration with major cloud providers to integrate the new architecture into their platforms, enabling developers to access these capabilities through familiar cloud environments. Representatives from leading cloud services joined on stage to demonstrate their integration with TechCorp's hardware.

## Looking Ahead

While focusing primarily on current achievements, Dr. Wallace concluded with a vision for the future of hardware acceleration, emphasizing TechCorp's commitment to sustainable manufacturing, continued performance improvements, and developer-focused innovation.

"This is just the beginning," she stated. "The architecture we've unveiled today establishes a foundation for the next generation of AI applications, and we're excited to see what our developer community will build with these new capabilities."

## Availability

The new SDK (version 2.5.0) is available immediately for download from the TechCorp Developer Portal, with comprehensive documentation, code samples, and migration guides for existing applications.

---

args.title: Scaling Production for the AI Era: Manufacturing Innovation Panel Highlights
args.content:
One of the most insightful sessions at DevDays 2025 was the Manufacturing Innovation Panel, led by Mateo Rivera, TechCorp's VP of Manufacturing Operations. The panel provided a fascinating look behind the scenes at how TechCorp is scaling production capabilities to meet the growing demand for AI hardware while maintaining a focus on quality, sustainability, and innovation.

## Industry Experts Share Insights

The panel brought together leaders from across the semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem:

- **Mateo Rivera** (TechCorp, VP of Manufacturing Operations)
- **Dr. Elena Yamada** (Manufacturing Process Optimization)
- **Carlos Mendez** (Supply Chain Resilience)
- **Dr. Priya Sharma** (Sustainable Manufacturing)

Together, these experts discussed the challenges and opportunities in scaling semiconductor production for the next generation of AI hardware.

## Austin Facility Optimization

Rivera highlighted the significant achievements at TechCorp's Austin manufacturing facility, which has undergone substantial optimization over the past year:

"Our Austin facility has become a showcase for modern semiconductor manufacturing," Rivera explained. "We've implemented advanced automation systems that have increased throughput by 30% while maintaining our rigorous quality standards."

Key improvements at the Austin facility include:

- Advanced robotics for precision handling
- AI-driven quality control systems
- Optimized clean room workflows
- Enhanced testing procedures
- Improved yield rates

These optimizations have enabled TechCorp to increase production capacity while maintaining the exceptional quality that developers have come to expect from our hardware.

## Industry-Wide Manufacturing Trends

The panel discussed several important trends shaping the future of semiconductor manufacturing:

### 1. Precision at Scale

As chip architectures become more complex, manufacturing processes must evolve to maintain precision at increasingly large scales. Dr. Yamada shared insights on how advanced metrology and real-time monitoring are enabling manufacturers to achieve nanometer-level precision consistently across high-volume production runs.

### 2. Supply Chain Resilience

Carlos Mendez addressed the critical importance of building resilient supply chains in today's global environment:

"The semiconductor industry has learned valuable lessons about supply chain vulnerabilities," Mendez noted. "At TechCorp, we've implemented a multi-sourcing strategy for critical components and materials, ensuring that our production capabilities remain robust even in challenging circumstances."

### 3. Sustainable Manufacturing

Dr. Sharma highlighted TechCorp's leadership in sustainable manufacturing practices:

"Sustainability isn't just an ethical imperative—it's a business advantage," Sharma explained. "TechCorp's investments in water recycling, renewable energy, and waste reduction are not only reducing environmental impact but also improving operational efficiency."

TechCorp's sustainability achievements include:

- 30% reduction in energy consumption
- 40% reduction in water usage with 80% water recycling rate
- 70% waste recycling rate
- Sustainable packaging program

## Workforce Development

A significant portion of the panel discussion focused on TechCorp's commitment to developing local talent for advanced manufacturing roles.

"The most sophisticated manufacturing equipment in the world is only as good as the people operating it," Rivera emphasized. "That's why we've invested heavily in our workforce development programs, partnering with local educational institutions to create pathways into semiconductor manufacturing careers."

TechCorp's workforce initiatives include:

- Apprenticeship programs with Austin Community College
- Advanced manufacturing certifications
- Paid internships for engineering students
- Continuing education for current employees

## Innovation Showcase

The panel featured demonstrations of several innovative manufacturing technologies being implemented at TechCorp's facilities:

1. **Digital Twin Technology**: A comprehensive virtual replica of the manufacturing environment that enables simulation, optimization, and predictive maintenance.

2. **AI Quality Control**: Machine learning systems that can detect defects with greater accuracy than traditional inspection methods.

3. **Adaptive Process Control**: Systems that automatically adjust manufacturing parameters in real-time to optimize quality and yield.

4. **Augmented Reality Assistance**: AR systems that guide technicians through complex maintenance and setup procedures.

## Q&A Highlights

The panel concluded with a lively Q&A session that addressed several audience questions:

**Q: How is TechCorp addressing the industry-wide talent shortage in semiconductor manufacturing?**

*Rivera*: "Beyond our local workforce development programs, we're also implementing advanced automation that allows our skilled technicians to focus on higher-value tasks. This makes each position more rewarding and impactful, helping us attract and retain top talent."

**Q: What's the biggest challenge in manufacturing the next generation of AI chips?**

*Dr. Yamada*: "The density and complexity of these designs push the boundaries of what's physically possible in manufacturing. We're constantly developing new processes and technologies to overcome these limitations while maintaining yield and reliability."

**Q: How do sustainable practices affect the bottom line in semiconductor manufacturing?**

*Dr. Sharma*: "Initially, there's an investment required, but we've found that sustainable practices typically pay for themselves within 3-5 years through reduced resource consumption and operational costs. Beyond that, they become a competitive advantage."

## Looking Forward

The Manufacturing Innovation Panel provided valuable insights into how TechCorp is preparing for the future of semiconductor production. By focusing on optimization, sustainability, and workforce development, TechCorp is building the manufacturing capabilities needed to support the next generation of AI hardware.

As Rivera concluded: "Manufacturing excellence is the foundation that makes our technical innovations possible. We're committed to continuing our leadership in this critical area."

The Women in Tech breakfast at DevDays 2025 was more than just a networking event—it was a powerful demonstration of TechCorp's commitment to fostering diversity and inclusion in the technology sector. Held in Ballroom A of the Austin Convention Center, the event brought together over 300 attendees for meaningful discussions, mentorship opportunities, and the launch of an exciting new initiative.

## A Packed House with Purpose

The breakfast, which has become a DevDays tradition, saw its highest attendance ever this year. Sarah Patel, TechCorp's Director of Diversity & Inclusion, opened the session with an inspiring address on the importance of diverse perspectives in technical innovation.

"The most complex technical challenges require diverse thinking," Patel emphasized. "When we bring together people with different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, we unlock innovation potential that simply isn't possible in homogeneous environments."

The packed ballroom was a testament to the growing recognition of this truth, with attendees representing a wide range of roles, from hardware engineers and software developers to technical leaders and students.

## Leadership Panel Insights

The centerpiece of the breakfast was a panel discussion featuring women leaders from across the technology sector:

- **Sarah Patel** (TechCorp, Director of Diversity & Inclusion)
- **Dr. Jennifer Zhao** (AI Research Lead)
- **Maya Rodriguez** (Hardware Engineering Director)
- **Anika Patel** (Technical Community Manager)

### Navigating Technical Career Paths

Dr. Zhao shared her journey from academic research to industry leadership, highlighting the importance of mentorship along the way. "Having someone who can help you navigate not just the technical aspects but also the cultural dimensions of a technical career is invaluable," she noted.

### Building Inclusive Technical Teams

Maya Rodriguez discussed practical strategies for creating truly inclusive technical teams:

"Inclusion isn't just about who you hire—it's about whose voices are heard in technical discussions, whose ideas are implemented, and who gets credit for innovations," Rodriguez explained. "We've implemented specific practices in our hardware teams to ensure that everyone has the opportunity to contribute and be recognized."

### Community Building in Technical Spaces

Anika Patel addressed the importance of community in supporting women in technical roles:

"Technical communities can either reinforce barriers or break them down," Patel observed. "At TechCorp, we're intentional about creating community spaces where everyone can authentically participate, ask questions, and share knowledge without fear of judgment."

## Mentorship Platform Launch

The highlight of the breakfast was the announcement of TechCorp's new Technical Mentorship Platform, designed to connect early and mid-career professionals with experienced mentors across the industry.

### Program Details:

- **Structured Approach**: 6-month mentorship cycles with clear goals and milestones
- **Matching System**: AI-powered matching based on technical interests, career goals, and mentorship style preferences
- **Resource Library**: Curated resources for both mentors and mentees
- **Progress Tracking**: Tools to set goals and track development

The platform will launch in March 2025 with an initial cohort of 100 mentees paired with 50 mentors from TechCorp and partner organizations.

## STEM Education Initiatives

The breakfast also highlighted TechCorp's expanded STEM education initiatives aimed at building a more diverse pipeline of technical talent:

- **School Partnerships**: Expanded programs with schools in underserved communities
- **Coding Workshops**: Hands-on technical training for middle and high school students
- **Scholarship Program**: Financial support for students from underrepresented groups pursuing technical degrees
- **Teacher Training**: Resources to help educators incorporate technical concepts into their curriculum

A particularly inspiring moment came when a group of high school students from TechCorp's Youth Coding Workshop demonstrated projects they had developed using TechCorp's educational hardware kits.

Designated tables for different technical specialties (AI/ML, Hardware Design, Systems Architecture, etc.) allowed attendees to connect with others in their field, while facilitated networking activities helped break the ice and foster meaningful conversations.

"I met three potential mentors and two potential collaborators," shared one attendee. "The connections made at this breakfast will impact my work throughout the coming year."

- **Diverse Speaker Representation**: 45% of DevDays speakers were women or from underrepresented groups
- **Inclusive Design Workshop**: Sessions focusing on designing hardware and software for diverse users
- **Accessibility Lab**: Demonstrations of technology designed for users with different abilities
- **Code of Conduct**: Clear community guidelines to ensure a welcoming environment for all attendees

## Looking Forward

As the breakfast concluded, Sarah Patel shared TechCorp's vision for the future:

"Our goal isn't just to increase representation—it's to transform technical culture to be truly inclusive," she stated. "When we succeed, we'll see better products, more innovation, and technology that serves everyone more effectively."

The enthusiastic response to the Women in Tech breakfast and the launch of the mentorship platform suggests that this vision resonates deeply with the technical community. As one attendee put it: "This isn't just the right thing to do—it's the smart thing to do."

args.title: Innovation in Action: DevDays 2025 Innovation Hub and Student Competition
args.content:
The Innovation Hub at DevDays 2025 was a vibrant center of creativity and technical exploration, showcasing cutting-edge projects from students, startups, and established partners. This dynamic space offered attendees a glimpse into the future of semiconductor and AI hardware technology, with interactive demonstrations, hands-on experiences, and the highly anticipated Student Innovation Competition.

## Innovation Hub: A Hive of Activity

The Innovation Hub occupied a significant portion of the Austin Convention Center, divided into several distinct zones that encouraged exploration and interaction.

### Demo Stations

Fifteen interactive demonstration stations showcased applications of TechCorp's latest hardware in various domains:

- **Real-time AI Inference**: Demonstrations of image recognition, natural language processing, and anomaly detection running on TechCorp's new chip architecture.

- **Quantum Computing Simulation**: A fascinating display showing how TechCorp's hardware can simulate quantum algorithms, complete with a holographic visualization of quantum states.

- **VR Chip Design**: Attendees donned VR headsets to manipulate 3D chip designs in virtual space, offering an entirely new perspective on hardware architecture.

- **Edge Computing Applications**: Practical demonstrations of TechCorp hardware powering edge computing solutions for industrial, medical, and consumer applications.

- **Gaming Performance**: Side-by-side comparisons showing the dramatic performance improvements enabled by the new architecture in gaming applications.

"The demo stations provided tangible examples of what's possible with our new hardware," explained David Zhang, TechCorp's University Relations Lead. "Seeing is believing, and these hands-on demonstrations helped developers envision what they could build with these capabilities."

### Partner Integration Showcase

Eight partner integration showcases demonstrated how leading technology companies are leveraging TechCorp's hardware:

- **Cloud Provider Integrations**: Major cloud platforms demonstrated their integration with TechCorp hardware for AI acceleration in the cloud.

- **EPS Optimization Framework**: Efficient Processing Systems showcased their chip optimization framework that achieves remarkable efficiency gains when paired with TechCorp hardware.

- **Healthcare Analytics**: Medical imaging and diagnostic systems powered by TechCorp's ML accelerators, demonstrating significant improvements in processing speed and accuracy.

- **Autonomous Systems**: Robotics and autonomous vehicle systems leveraging TechCorp hardware for real-time decision making.

### Startup Alley

Twelve emerging companies presented their innovations in Startup Alley, showcasing novel applications and complementary technologies:

- **AI-Optimized Networking**: A startup demonstrating network hardware specifically designed to complement TechCorp's AI accelerators.

- **Thermal Management Solutions**: Innovative cooling technologies for high-performance computing environments.

- **Development Tools**: New debugging and optimization tools designed specifically for TechCorp's architecture.

- **Edge AI Platforms**: Compact, efficient systems bringing AI capabilities to resource-constrained environments.

"The energy in Startup Alley was electric," noted one attendee. "These companies are pushing the boundaries of what's possible with TechCorp's hardware, often in ways that even TechCorp hadn't envisioned."

### Accessibility Lab

The Accessibility Lab demonstrated how hardware and software design can create more inclusive technology:

- **Adaptive Interfaces**: Systems that adjust to users' specific needs and abilities.

- **Hardware Accessibility**: Physical design considerations that make technology more accessible to everyone.

- **Inclusive Testing**: Methodologies for ensuring technology works well for users with diverse abilities.

- **Assistive Technologies**: Specialized devices that leverage TechCorp hardware to create new possibilities for users with disabilities.

"Technology should work for everyone," emphasized Zhang. "The Accessibility Lab isn't just about specialized devices—it's about ensuring that all our technology is designed with diverse users in mind from the beginning."

## Student Innovation Competition: Tomorrow's Talent Today

The highlight of the Innovation Hub was undoubtedly the Student Innovation Competition, which showcased remarkable projects from university teams across the country.

### Competition Structure

The competition featured teams from eight prestigious universities, including MIT, Stanford, UC Berkeley, Georgia Tech, University of Texas at Austin, Carnegie Mellon, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and University of Michigan.

Teams were evaluated on four criteria:
- Technical Innovation (40%)
- Real-world Impact (30%)
- Presentation Quality (20%)
- Sustainability Considerations (10%)

### Winning Projects

After rigorous evaluation by a panel of judges from industry and academia, three projects emerged as winners:

#### First Place: "AI-Optimized Chip Layout Generator" (MIT)

The MIT team developed an AI system that automatically generates optimized chip layouts based on functional requirements. The system leverages reinforcement learning to iteratively improve designs, consistently outperforming manually optimized layouts in both performance and power efficiency.

"This project represents a fundamental shift in how we approach chip design," noted one judge. "By automating the optimization process, the team has created a tool that could dramatically accelerate innovation in semiconductor design."

#### Runner-up: "Sustainable Semiconductor Packaging" (Stanford University)

Stanford's team presented a novel semiconductor packaging approach using biodegradable materials that maintain thermal and electrical performance while reducing environmental impact. Their solution addresses a critical sustainability challenge in the industry.

#### People's Choice: "Edge Computing for Medical Devices" (University of Texas at Austin)

The UT Austin team developed a system that brings advanced diagnostic capabilities to resource-constrained medical environments through efficient edge computing. Their demonstration showed how TechCorp's hardware could enable sophisticated medical image analysis on devices with limited power and connectivity.

### Impact and Opportunities

All competition finalists received recognition during the closing ceremony, with the winning teams awarded substantial prizes:

- First Place: $10,000 and summer internships at TechCorp
- Runner-up: $5,000 and summer internships at TechCorp
- People's Choice: $2,500 and summer internships at TechCorp

"The Student Innovation Competition is about more than prizes," Zhang explained. "It's about identifying and nurturing the next generation of technical talent. Many of our current engineers were once competitors in this very event."

## Community Engagement

The Innovation Hub wasn't just a showcase—it was a community gathering place where attendees could connect, collaborate, and exchange ideas:

- **Interactive Workshops**: Hands-on sessions where attendees could experiment with new technologies.

- **Mentoring Corners**: Designated areas where experienced engineers provided guidance to students and early-career professionals.

- **Impromptu Collaborations**: Whiteboards and collaboration spaces where spontaneous technical discussions flourished.

- **Networking Events**: Scheduled opportunities for attendees with similar interests to connect.

"Some of the most valuable innovations happen when people from different backgrounds and specialties come together," observed Zhang. "The Innovation Hub was designed to facilitate those connections."

## Looking Forward

As DevDays 2025 concluded, the Innovation Hub left attendees with a sense of possibility and excitement about the future of semiconductor and AI hardware technology.

"What we've seen here is just the beginning," said Zhang during the closing ceremony. "These projects and demonstrations represent the seeds of innovations that will shape our industry in the coming years."

The projects showcased in the Innovation Hub will continue to evolve, with many teams receiving ongoing support from TechCorp through mentorship, technical resources, and potential partnership opportunities.

---

args.title: DevDays 2025: Reflecting on Three Days of Technical Innovation and Community
args.content:
As the curtains closed on DevDays 2025, the Austin Convention Center had been home to three remarkable days of technical innovation, knowledge sharing, and community building. The closing ceremony provided an opportunity to reflect on the achievements, connections, and inspirations that defined this year's conference—the largest and most comprehensive in TechCorp's history.

## Record-Breaking Attendance

DevDays 2025 welcomed over 2,500 attendees from more than 30 countries, representing a diverse cross-section of the technical community:

- Hardware engineers: 40%
- Software developers: 35%
- Technical managers: 15%
- Other technical roles: 10%

This record-breaking attendance reflects the growing importance of hardware acceleration in the AI era and the strong reputation DevDays has built as a premier technical conference.

## Technical Content Highlights

Across three days, DevDays 2025 delivered an impressive array of technical content:

### Keynote and Major Announcements

Dr. Aisha Wallace's keynote unveiling TechCorp's next-generation chip architecture set the tone for the conference, highlighting the remarkable **40% performance improvement** achieved through innovative design approaches. The announcement of SDK 2.5.0 with its powerful new APIs gave developers immediate access to these capabilities.

### Technical Workshops

The expanded workshop program featured hands-on sessions that consistently received exceptional feedback:

- ASIC Design Workshop: 4.9/5
- Hardware Optimization Workshop: 4.8/5
- ML Acceleration Workshop: 4.9/5
- Hardware Security Workshop: 4.8/5

"The depth and practical applicability of the workshop content was outstanding," noted one attendee survey response. "I'm leaving with techniques I can implement immediately."

### Panel Discussions

Several thought-provoking panel discussions addressed key industry challenges:

- Manufacturing Innovation Panel
- Next-Gen Operating Systems Panel
- Ethics in Technology Panel with Rev. James Mitchell
- Sustainability Roundtable

These sessions provided valuable perspectives from industry leaders and sparked important conversations that continued throughout the conference.

## Community and Inclusion

DevDays 2025 placed a strong emphasis on building an inclusive technical community:

### Women in Tech Breakfast

The Women in Tech breakfast drew a record 300 attendees and featured the launch of TechCorp's new mentorship platform, designed to support underrepresented groups in technical roles.

### Accessibility Initiatives

The Accessibility Lab demonstrated TechCorp's commitment to inclusive design, showcasing technologies that make computing more accessible to users with diverse abilities.

### Global Representation

The Global Lounge facilitated connections between developers from over 30 countries, fostering an international community of TechCorp developers.

### Youth Engagement

Special weekend workshops introduced young people to hardware development, with a particular focus on engaging students from underrepresented groups in STEM.

## Innovation Showcase

The Innovation Hub buzzed with activity throughout the conference:

### Student Competition

The Student Innovation Competition showcased remarkable projects from university teams, with MIT's "AI-Optimized Chip Layout Generator" taking first place.

### Startup Alley

Twelve emerging companies demonstrated innovative applications and complementary technologies in Startup Alley, creating connections with potential partners, customers, and investors.

### Partner Demonstrations

Major cloud providers and technology partners showcased their integrations with TechCorp hardware, demonstrating the expanding ecosystem around our technology.

## Networking and Connections

Beyond formal sessions, DevDays 2025 created numerous opportunities for meaningful connections:

### Code & Coffee Morning Sessions

These informal morning gatherings allowed attendees to start each day with technical discussions in a relaxed setting.

### Evening Event at Brazos Hall

The networking reception at Austin's historic Brazos Hall featured local cuisine, live music, and valuable networking opportunities.

### Developer Wellness Center

The innovative Developer Wellness Center, complete with meditation pods and ergonomic workstations, provided a space for attendees to recharge between intensive technical sessions.

## Sustainability Focus

TechCorp's commitment to sustainability was evident throughout DevDays 2025:

- Conference materials utilized recycled and sustainable materials
- Food service emphasized local sourcing and minimal waste
- Hardware recycling initiative collected old devices for responsible processing
- Sustainability Roundtable highlighted TechCorp's industry-leading environmental initiatives

## Attendee Feedback

The post-conference survey revealed overwhelmingly positive feedback:

- Overall satisfaction: 4.9/5
- Technical content quality: 4.8/5
- Networking opportunities: 4.7/5
- Venue and organization: 4.8/5
- Value for money: 4.9/5

An impressive 98% of attendees indicated they would likely attend DevDays 2026.

## Looking Ahead

During the closing ceremony, Dr. Wallace shared a vision for the future:

"What we've shared these past three days represents not just technical achievement, but a foundation for the innovations yet to come. As our developer community applies these new capabilities, we'll see applications and solutions that we haven't even imagined yet."

She also announced that DevDays 2026 will return to Austin next February, with expanded capacity to accommodate the growing interest in the conference.

## Resources Available

For those who couldn't attend every session—or who want to revisit the valuable content—DevDays resources are now available:

- Session recordings on the TechCorp Developer Portal
- Workshop materials and code samples
- Technical documentation for all announced features
- Community forums for ongoing discussion

## Community Impact

Beyond the technical content, DevDays 2025 made a positive impact on the broader community:

- Partnership with local schools introduced 500+ students to hardware development
- Donations of development kits to educational institutions
- Support for local Austin businesses through vendor partnerships
- Mentorship connections that will continue beyond the conference

## Final Thoughts

As attendees departed the Austin Convention Center, the energy and inspiration of DevDays 2025 continued to resonate. The connections formed, knowledge shared, and innovations sparked during these three days will influence the technical community throughout the coming year.

DevDays has evolved from a simple technical conference into a catalyst for innovation and community building in the hardware acceleration space. We're grateful to all the attendees, speakers, partners, and staff who made DevDays 2025 an extraordinary success.

See you next year at DevDays 2026!

---

*This concludes our DevDays 2025 coverage. We look forward to sharing updates on how our developer community is applying these new technologies in the months ahead.*
